lines.text: Half the grain was gone. Thirty-seven people would be hungry by midwinter. So I went back to my books.
Chapter eleven of On the Management of Northern Estates. Glasshouses, and the forcing of vegetables in cold climates. The author had never seen rimeglass. I had a forge full of it.
You want me to bury rimeglass in the dirt? My lord, that's two hundred crowns a lamp!
Not lamps. Slivers. The shavings you sweep off the floor. Buried under a glass roof, they'll keep the soil warm all winter.
That's either genius, or madness.
With him, it's usually both.
We built the first glasshouse against the south wall of the keep. Old windows from the ruined half of the castle, and rimeglass shavings in the soil beneath.
Wren's mother planted turnips. Everyone laughed. Turnips, in the dead of winter.
Nine days later, the turnips came up.
That's not possible. Turnips take two months. Even in summer.
Good soil.
Stop saying that.
By the end of the month we had four glasshouses. Turnips, cabbages, beans. Nobody would starve this winter.
And the strange cold in my bones, the one that began the night of the fire, faded. I slept well for the first time in weeks.
That was the week the scholar arrived.
Good afternoon. My name is Ilse, a travelling scholar from the Royal Academy. I'm writing a survey of northern farming. Might I stay a few days?
She had kind eyes behind round spectacles, a satchel full of notebooks, and very cold hands.
Of course. We have turnips.
She asked a great many questions. About the soil. About the mill. About the villagers.
She asked to shake hands with everyone. Thirty-seven people. Every single one.
I thought it was a southern custom.
It wasn't.
Wren, the huntress. Three rings. Tobin, the blacksmith. Three rings. The old woman who carries the water. Two.
A village of commoners, where the commoners don't stay common.
And the lord himself. Nothing. The lens doesn't even flicker.
Outside her window, Bram stood in the snow, watching her candle burn late into the night.
Scholar. My one remaining arm.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter six, coming soon.
